hero.heading: Web development for products people keep using.
hero.subtitle: I design and build the interface, the backend, and the release path as one system. The result is a site or app you can change without starting over.

overview: This is for a new site, a rebuild, or a product that has outgrown a page builder. I work from the flows your customers and team use, then implement them in a stack that stays understandable.
problem: A lot of web projects start from a template. The first version looks finished, then every real requirement — accounts, content, payments, search — turns into a plugin pile that is slow and hard to change.
solution: I scope a first release that covers the real journeys, build it in Next.js and TypeScript, and keep the content model and the interface in the same codebase so later features have a place to land.

features.title: A clear information model
features.detail: Pages, collections, and accounts match the business, so editors are not fighting the CMS.

features.title: Fast public pages
features.detail: The important routes are server-rendered and cached where it helps, so the first view is quick.

features.title: Room to grow
features.detail: Auth, payments, and integrations are added as parts of the product, not as afterthoughts.

process.title: Discovery
process.detail: We pin down the outcome, the constraints, and what the first release has to do.

process.title: Planning
process.detail: I turn that into a scope, a sequence, and the technical approach.

process.title: Development
process.detail: I build in small slices you can review, on the stack this service uses.

process.title: Testing
process.detail: We check the flows that matter before anything is treated as finished.

process.title: Launch
process.detail: I ship it, watch the first days, and leave you with a clear way to change it.

benefits.title: One codebase
benefits.detail: Design, content, and logic live together, so a change does not mean three tools.

benefits.title: Honest scope
benefits.detail: The first release is the part people will actually use, not a catalogue of screens.

benefits.title: You can ship again
benefits.detail: The handoff includes how to edit, deploy, and add the next feature.

faqs.question: Do you rebuild existing sites?
faqs.answer: Yes. We keep what is working, replace what is slowing you down, and move content across with a plan instead of a surprise.

faqs.question: Can my team edit the content?
faqs.answer: Yes. The editing path is part of the build, whether that is a CMS, a simple admin, or files your team already understands.
